Thanks again for hosting the ACME team at our SF workshop last week — great progress on the rollout plan. Two quick items on the travel side before I file expenses:

1) I used my personal card for a dinner that was billed to a shared corporate card afterward; there's a discrepancy on the corporate card statement with a duplicate-looking charge dated 09/03. Can TravelOps confirm whether that was a merchant duplicate or an internal processing issue?

2) For reimbursements: will Redwood do direct ACH to my account or should I submit via the expense portal (I can attach the receipts if needed)? I want to confirm the preferred path so ACME's procurement team can reconcile on their end too.

Attaching boarding pass and a consolidated PDF of hotel receipts for now. I'll push a completed CSV expense report once I reconcile per diem vs actuals.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Great to hear from you and glad the workshop went well. On our side: I see a charge for the dinner at "The Bayroom" on 09/03 for $432.50 and a separate corporate-billed line for $432.50; our AP team flagged that as likely a duplicate authorization that cleared separately. I've looped in accounts-payable so they can confirm whether they pushed a charge-back or submitted a reimbursement to your card by mistake.

For reconciliation, our procurement prefers you submit the expense report and we will match to the PO. If Redwood will do an internal ACH to you, please confirm — otherwise we can coordinate a one-time invoice credit on our end once AP resolves the duplicate.

Sarah

Marissa — thanks for flagging this quickly. A few notes from finance: 

1) Reimbursement path: We can reimburse you directly (ACH) for the personal dinner charge. Please submit the expense via Concur/Expense portal and select "Personal CC reimbursement". Since ACME also charged a corporate card, we'll hold off final settlement until we confirm whether ACME issues a credit. If ACME credits us, we'll process offsetting entries rather than double-pay you.

2) Corporate card anomaly: Please upload the card statement page showing the corporate charge and your itemized receipt (merchant receipt). We'll open a dispute with the card provider if the merchant confirms it was a duplicate charge. Monica, can you help with the dispute workflow and confirm the GL code for the event hospitality so Marissa is routed correctly?

3) Timing: If you submit today, expect reimbursement within 7–10 business days (standard ACH). If ACME resolves in our favor (credit), we'll update your reimbursement to net-zero and notify you.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick update:

- I opened a merchant dispute with our card provider this morning referencing TXN-8891023 and uploaded the merchant receipt you provided. Case #CARD-2025-7342.
- I reviewed your Concur submission and approved the reimbursement for $432.50 under GL code 6421-Event Hospitality; finance will issue ACH on 2025-09-10.
- If ACME issues a credit to our corporate card after their AP review, we will reverse the reimbursement and notify you immediately. If reimbursement reversal is required, we'll coordinate for the net settlement (we will not leave you out of pocket; any reversal will be handled as an adjustment on our payroll/AR).

Closing notes: please keep receipts for 90 days per policy and forward any correspondence from ACME AP if they confirm the duplicate charge. Thanks for capturing evidence promptly — made the whole process much smoother.
